children: Shares of Mahanadi Coalfields, the largest coal producing subsidiary of State-run coal behemoth Coal India, on Friday made a muted debut on stock exchanges and ended with a discount of nearly 3 per cent against the issue price of  ₹136.
On the NSE, the stock made its debut at  ₹134, registering a discount of 1.47 per cent. It ended at  ₹132.50 apiece, around 2.57 per cent below the issue price.

On the BSE, the shares closed at  ₹132.60 apiece, down 2.5 per cent from the issue price and 0.41 per cent below the opening price of  ₹133.15. During the day, the stock hit the day’s low of  ₹130.70, lower by 3.89 per cent.
Market valuation of Mahanadi Coalfields (MCL), which is the single largest coal producing firm in India in terms of production in FY26, stood at  ₹87,759.49 crore.

“The (investors’) response to IPO indicates (they) may not be that gung-ho about Coal India or its subsidiaries that are into conventional coal production,” said Arun Kejriwal, founder at Kejriwal Research & Investment Services.
Cholamandalam Securities said in a note last week that Mahanadi Coalfields faces structural challenges from the gradual transition towards renewable energy.

The initial public offering (IPO) of MCL was subscribed 1.52 times on the final day of bidding on Monday. The issue received bids of 74,86,87,060 equity shares against the offered 49,30,68,045 equity shares.

MCL is the third Coal India subsidiary to tap the public markets this year. Coal India has already listed Bharat Coking Coal Ltd in January, while the IPO of Central Mine Planning & Design Institute Ltd concluded in March.

“Mahanadi Coalfields Limited has been listed on BSE Ltd and National Stock Exchange of India Ltd effective November 27, 2026. As a result, the company’s shareholding in Mahanadi Coalfields stands reduced from 100 per cent to 90 per cent of the issued and paid-up equity share capital of Mahanadi Coalfields Limited,” Coal India said in a stock exchange filing.
“Consequent to the above, Mahanadi Coalfields ceases to be a wholly owned subsidiary of the company. However, it continues to remain a subsidiary of the company,” CIL added.
Incorporated in 1992, MCL produced 218.31 million tonnes of coal in FY26, accounting for around 22.4 per cent of India’s total non-coking coal production.

title: Mahanadi Coalfields shares make muted debut on stock exchanges
